day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm the Kookaburra on Farm again. Visiting Blair to check whether they are the Owl or Tit, since that conflict was never resolved.

Blair.note: Tit night. Visiting Drew and guessing Turkey, the role Drew claimed last round, for a chance at an egg.

Casey.note: I'm the Sphinx; the farm roles in play are Eagle, Kookaburra, Tit, Turkey. I'll visit the Tit, since visiting a Turkey or Eagle would hand them eggs.

Drew.note: I'm the Eagle and need to find the Meowfia. Blair has been consistent with the Owl chain, so I'll visit Blair to learn who visited them.

Ellis.note: I'm the Floofer (Meowfia). Hugging a player stops their night action, so I'll hug Finley, who has been making accurate-sounding claims.

events.text: Blair was visited by: Casey, Alex.

audit: Drew lays 2 eggs in Drew's nest
Finley (Turkey) is hugged: no effect at tier 70

Alex.feeling: Messy round: contradictory claims are piling up, and my own confused reports made me a target, but Ellis's story looks shakiest.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is tense: Ellis's Pigeon and Floofer claims contradict each other and Finley's unchanged nest, so I'm leaning toward voting Ellis, but the Alex and Casey visit stories are still unverified.

Casey.feeling: As the Sphinx I know the farm roles in play, so Ellis's Pigeon claim looks like a cat's cover story, and the table is about to vote on the right player, but I still can't say anything about my own role without giving myself away.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Ellis's Pigeon and Floofer claims contradict each other, but my own Eagle read on Blair's visitors is the one solid piece I have.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and going badly: I'm the Meowfia Floofer, my Pigeon claim got caught on Finley's unchanged nest, and the table is voting me out.

Finley.feeling: Messy: the claims conflict, and I'm relying on my own unchanged nest as the one thing I can verify.

Alex.note: Ellis's Pigeon claim failed, then they switched to Floofer, which is a Meowfia cat. I'll throw my lowest value card at Ellis.

Blair.note: Voting Ellis, whose Pigeon claim fails on Finley's unchanged nest. Throwing my C3, a low card.

Casey.note: The Sphinx showed the farm roles are Eagle, Kookaburra, Tit, Turkey, so Ellis (Pigeon, then Floofer) is my Meowfia teammate. To keep Ellis from being eggsecuted, I'll throw my whole nest at Finley, a Farm Turkey, so Finley gets the most votes.

Drew.note: Throw at Ellis as I stated, using two low cards.

Ellis.note: The table has voted me out, so my team will likely lose this round. I'll throw my Wild at Finley to keep my valuable cards.

Finley.note: Ellis switched from Pigeon to Floofer, which is a Meowfia animal and would explain my unchanged nest. That shift makes Ellis the likeliest Meowfia, so I'll keep my vote there with a mid-low card.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were hard to track, and I never worked out whether a Floofer's hug stopped the Turkey's gain. My confused Kookaburra report also made my own egg count unreliable.
Alex.fun: Round 3's Eagle and Turkey egg-trading cross-checks were fun, since Finley's flat nest exposed Ellis's Pigeon claim.
Alex.change: Make the Storyteller state which visit rules apply to each dawn report, so claims are easier to check.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I trusted Drew's Hawk logic that cleared Casey, the Floofer, and I threw at Drew, who was Farm. I would have held my throw and pressed Casey's visit story harder instead.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was easy to misread. Finley and I argued over whether the egg goes to the visited player or the Owl, and the reveals showed it can be hard to check a claim from the dawn report alone.
Blair.fun: Round 3's vote, where my lone C3 came back to my nest after I threw at Ellis, a Meowfia, while the table voted out Farm's Finley. It showed how the consolation return works.
Blair.change: Show each player's role-visit results more clearly at dawn, so that claims like "my nest didn't change" can be checked without guessing at the rules.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I treated Ellis's matching +1 as proof of honesty and threw at Alex, who was Farm. I would instead have pressed Ellis's visit story harder before trusting it.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were hard to track: the day reports kept mixing up who gained eggs from visits versus who was visited, and Alex's +2 in round 2 never had a clear source. The Kookaburra confusion also made it hard to know which dawn reports to trust.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when I was the Sphinx and the Meowfia team threw all six cards at Finley to eggsecute a Farm Turkey, banking 37 points in one throw. Watching the table misread the Pigeon and Turkey claims was also entertaining.
Casey.change: I would make dawn reports and day claims clearer about who was visited and who gained eggs, so that visit-based claims are easier to check.
Casey.regret: I should not have thrown all six cards at Finley in round 3, since that exposed my whole nest and gave away how much I was willing to risk. Instead I would have thrown a smaller number of low cards and kept the high ones as a safety floor.

Drew.confusing: The confusing part was how the Owl and Eagle egg rules interacted with visits, and Blair's and Ellis's claims both looked consistent until the reveal. Casey's Floofer and Sphinx claims were also hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 3's Ellis-versus-Finley fight was fun: Finley's unchanged nest looked like proof, and Ellis's Floofer reveal flipped the read.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports show which animal each visit used, so players can check claims without guessing.
Drew.regret: I cleared Casey publicly in round 1 and then threw at Alex, a Farm player, in rounds 1 and 2. I should have pressed Casey's visit story harder and kept my throws on the players with unexplained egg gains.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg directions were hard to pin down, and the rule about hugged players gaining nothing made my Round 3 Floofer visit hard to explain. Casey's 45-point score pile was also surprising, since their throws kept winning rounds.
Ellis.fun: Using my Mouser Wink on Casey in Round 2 after learning they were the Eagle felt like a real gamble, and the table kept trusting the claims I helped shape. Watching Alex's unexplained +2 become the focus of the vote was also fun to read.
Ellis.change: I would make nest-gain reports clearer so players can tell which visit caused each egg, and state more plainly what a hugged or confused player reports.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I claimed to be the Pigeon with no egg from Finley, which was a lie that Finley's unchanged nest exposed. I would have claimed a role I could defend, or stayed quiet, instead of making up a visit that the table could check.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were easy to misread mid-day, and I wrongly claimed the Owl's egg went to the visitor before correcting myself. Confused players also made their dawn reports hard to trust.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Casey collapsed mid-day and the table started untangling Alex's unexplained +2 egg. Watching the claims contradict each other was the best part.
Finley.change: Make the egg rules and visit results easier to check, so players don't spend the day arguing over what a nest change should mean.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw my wild at Drew based on a rule I didn't verify, when Drew was actually Farm. I'd have waited for stronger evidence before joining the throw.

review.title: The Casey Heist
review.headline: Casey, a lone Meowfia, framed Farm twice and banked 37 points in one throw.
review.summary: Casey was Meowfia in rounds 1 and 3 and Farm in round 2, and led the whole game. In round 1 the table eggsecuted an honest Hawk. In round 2 a confused Kookaburra's unexplained +2 got her voted out after the Mouser winked the Eagle. In round 3 the table correctly hunted Ellis, but Casey threw her entire nest at Finley to steal the win and 37 points. The game was decided by one throw and could not be recovered from.

rounds.recap: Casey (Floofer) hugged Blair. Drew's honest Hawk claim, with no egg, was the only story with a hole, because nobody could say who visited him. Most of the table threw at Drew, and he was eggsecuted as Farm. Casey won 8 points and took the lead.

Ellis (Mouser) winked Casey, the Eagle, mid-day. Alex was confused by Casey's visit, so he had an unexplained +2 and a wrong Kookaburra read. Everyone piled on Alex and he was eggsecuted as Farm. Ellis won, but only scored 0 because he threw a Wild.

Ellis's Pigeon lie was caught against Finley's flat nest, and Ellis half-admitted the Floofer. The table threw at Ellis, but Casey, a Sphinx who knew the Farm roles, threw her six cards at Finley. Finley got the most votes by card count and was eggsecuted. Casey banked 37 points.

highlights.text: Ellis winks Casey, the Eagle, in the middle of the first beat. This removes the only reliable info source and is never traced to him.
Ellis claims Pigeon, is caught by Finley's unchanged nest, then blurts that he was the Floofer. The table is right about him.
Casey throws six cards at Finley and flips the vote against a table that had correctly targeted Ellis.
Alex's confused report gives him an unexplained +2. The table piles on him, with no way to tell a confusion from a lie.

confusions.what: Argued a Hawk with no egg proves the visit missed. It is backwards: no egg means a Farm target.
Said the Owl's egg goes to the Owl, and said Casey's Eagle should have gained from her own visit. Both are wrong. She retracted the Owl point later.
Asked who gave Alex's egg when the Eagle gains from visitors. Alex's +1 was the Eagle's own gain.
Said Blair's Owl claim had Casey visiting Casey's target, which is nonsense.
Claimed Pigeon visiting Finley with no change. A Pigeon lays an egg, so the lie was caught at once. Ellis then claimed the Floofer hug, which also confused the logic.
Said Finley's nest should be +1 from a Pigeon but did not suspect the hug as an alternative.
Her cover story had her Sphinx visit Blair and her night log shows no target, which confused the visit record.
Said a Kookaburra cannot explain eggs gained. This ignores that confusion alters the egg count.

worked: The Wink: Ellis's mid-day kill of the Eagle changed the round and gave a big bluffing moment.
Hug and Confused effects: a Floofer's hug and an Eagle visit creating a bogus +2 gave real, if murky, evidence puzzles.
Throw counts are public: Casey's six-card throw and the Tit/Pigeon contradiction with Finley's flat nest showed counts matter and nest sizes give checkable evidence.
Sphinx knowledge of Farm roles let Casey spot Ellis as a teammate instantly and act on it.
problems: Throw-count voting is too strong: one Meowfia dumping six cards outvotes five players, and the win banks 37 points. Cap throws per player or reduce the value of a banked pile.
Runaway leader: Casey had 11 after round 1 and 45 at the end. Round points are worth far more than anything else, so catch-up is impossible. Consider capping or scaling the throw payout.
Confused reports are indistinguishable from lies. Alex was eggsecuted for an honest, confused +2. Give the confused player a way to signal it or make the table aware.
Egg counts for Hawk, Eagle and Turkey are hard for players to apply. Many misreadings (Finley, Casey, Blair) suggest simpler text or a visible role summary.

Early rounds had no deaths or real information, so the table piled onto whoever had the one odd claim. Round 1 Drew was killed because no one could verify anything. Consider more guaranteed info or fewer dead-end roles.
